name: ARO-ALK7
lead: ARO-ALK7 is an investigational RNA interference (RNAi) therapy directed at ALK7, a receptor involved in fat-cell signalling. It is being tested in adults with obesity, with and without type 2 diabetes, and its relevance to appearance is body fat: if it lowers fat-cell signalling as intended, the outcome of interest is reduced fat mass and a leaner build. It is not approved for any use [1].

The sole clinical information is a trial registration: a Phase 1/2 first-in-human study (NCT06937203) that began on 9 May 2025, is recruiting, and plans to enroll 150 adults [1]. No results have been reported.

On the biology, a 2025 review describes activin E and its adipocyte receptor pathway as regulators of fat-cell lipolysis and diet-induced obesity [2], and a 2026 preprint reports that deleting GDF3, an antagonist of the ActE/ALK7 pathway, reduced adipose lipolysis in obese mice [3].
infobox: Obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes

paras: RNAi drugs lower production of a chosen protein by silencing its gene; here the target is ALK7. Research on the activin E to ALK7 pathway in adipocytes is reviewed in the literature [2], and animal work on the pathway is ongoing [3].

One Phase 1/2 first-in-human trial is registered in adults with obesity with or without type 2 diabetes. It started on 9 May 2025, is recruiting, and has a target enrollment of 150.[1] No results have been identified.

timeline.event: Phase 1/2 first-in-human trial in obesity begins (May).[1]

card.summary: An experimental RNAi drug against ALK7 for obesity; a single early trial is recruiting and no results exist.
card.note: Investigational only; no published human data.

quick.overview:
ARO-ALK7 is an experimental RNA interference drug aimed at the ALK7 gene, being tested for obesity in a first-in-human trial.

No results have been published, so its effects are unknown.
quick.mechanism: RNAi drugs lower production of a chosen protein by silencing its gene; here the target is ALK7.
quick.risks: No safety data have been reported. The drug is investigational and not available by prescription.

chain: RNAi lowers ALK7 production in fat cells
Possible reduction in fat mass (under study)
angle.text: ARO-ALK7 is being tested for obesity, where the intended outcome is less body fat. Whether it changes fat mass in people is not yet known.
